land.text: Bone, which 'lost its independence to the Dutch' after the 1905 South Sulawesi expeditions and came under direct administration

successors.note: The Dutch restored a royal ruler in 1931 (Mappanyuki, 'a scion of both the houses of Gowa and Bone') and the sultan joined Indonesia in May 1950; that self-governing phase belongs on the Dutch East Indies and Indonesia dossiers.

wars.name: Makassar War
wars.outcome: Bone's Bugis under Arung Palakka fought with the VOC; the Treaty of Bungaya (18 November 1667) and the fall of Somba Opu in June 1669 made Bone 'the supreme principality in South Sulawesi'.
wars.note: The contest zone is Gowa's and is recorded in the Gowa dossier. The page: 'On 12 October 1668, the VOC-Bugis forces defeated the Gowa forces in a major battle in Makassar'.

wars.name: Dutch wars against Bone
wars.outcome: Bone fought the Dutch in 1824, 1859 and 1905; the 1905 expeditions ended its independence.
wars.note: The pages opened give no territorial result for 1824 or 1859.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey fixes Bone's boundary; the page gives the capital, the area ('about 2,600 km2') and the neighbours (Wajo, Soppeng allies, Luwu a rival over the Cenrana River mouth) but no line.

notes: Cliopatria 'Sultanate of Bone' (3 shapes, 1512..1858); its Wikipedia field reads 'Sultan', which is the wrong article; the right page is 'Bone Sultanate' (the Wikipedia title in the dossier). (1) The three shapes are the same eight cells (1,983-2,155 km2) 25-55 km south-west of Watampone; none contains the capital, so each is adjusted by a 25 km disc round Watampone. The infobox area (about 2,600 km2) is ambiguous (Bone Regency is larger), so the corrected shape (about 3,000 km2) stays within the factor of two. (2) Start: the infobox says 14th century and the rulers' table starts 1350, the body says early 15th century; 1350 is used at confidence 1. (3) End: the page gives 1905; Cliopatria stops in 1858. The 1931-1950 restored sultanate (Mappanyuki, joined Indonesia in May 1950) is a Dutch-sanctioned self-government and is left to the Dutch East Indies and Indonesia dossiers. (4) Gowa's suzerainty over Bone 1611-1667 (invasion 1611, risings 1644 and 1660, king restored 1667) is carried as contests here and as a vassal pair in the Gowa dossier; the Bone page itself does not call Bone Gowa's vassal and describes the 1582 Tellumpocco'e alliance (Bone, Wajo, Soppeng) as mutual defence, which is an association and not territory. (5) Bone's overlordship of South Sulawesi 1669-1814 is a tint on the whole province outside Bone and Makassar; Wajo, Soppeng, Luwu, Gowa and the rest have no dossier (counterparts needing dossiers: Wajo, Soppeng, Luwu, Kingdom of Tallo). (6) The fetch tool returns a model summary of each page; quotation marks mean 'as the fetched text gave it'. Page budget 1-2: two pages opened.
